texts.preamble: Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Raja (1) In The High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur Order IN S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) Date of Order : 02.08.2016 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GOVERDHAN BARDHAR Mr. Chandraveer Singh, for the petitioner.
texts.facts: Brief facts, giving rise to this revision petition are that on 18.07.1986, the Food Inspector inspected the shop of Bodu Khan situated at Bus Stand Beri Khurd and found that he was selling the food products without having the food licence. On the complaint, cognizance under Section 16/50 of PFA Act was S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) taken against the accused Bodu Khan and he was summoned. The accused Bodu Khan filed an application on 14.02.1992 stating that his name is Riyasat Ali and not Bodu Khan. Investigation in this regard was carried out and the trial court on 13/09/1993 reached on the conclusion that Bodu Khan and Riyasat Ali was one and the same person and rejected the petitioner's application. Thereafter, before framing of charge, statement of Mahipal Sharma (PW-1) was recorded. The learned trial Court framed charge against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 16/50 of PFA Act. The accused denied the charge and claimed for trial. After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned trial Court, the accused-petitioner approached the learned appellate Court.
texts.arguments: At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) that he is not challenging the conviction of the petitioner for offence Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of PFA Act read with Rule 50 of PFA Rules recorded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned appellate court but his only prayer is for issuance of direction to the State Government to consider case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, his case for commutation of sentence can very well be considered by the Government under Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. In support of this plea, learned counsel has placed reliance on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court in the case of N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food 4 Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80] and Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544]. Learned Public Prosecutor has not opposed the prayer in general and submitted that in some of the identical cases, directions have been issued by the Court for consideration of commutation of sentence. It is not disputed that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, the prayer to examine the case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence is acceptable. In N.Sukumaran (supra), Supreme Court examined the matter on the touchstone of Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. and held : "3. The offence took place in the year 1984. , "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the Riyasat Wali Khan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187153858/ 2 matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedures." A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Deva(supra) following the verdict in N.Sukumaran (supra) and taking into account the fact that incident is too old, held as under : Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C. On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 of Cr.P.C. Till then the petitioner will remain on same bail bonds." In this view of the matter and considering the S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.531/1996 (Riyasat Ali Khan @ Bundu Khan Vs. State of Rajasthan) fact that the incident has occurred about 30 years back, I deem it just and appropriate to direct the petitioner to deposit a sum of Rs.7,500/- as fine before learned trial Court in commutation of sentence of one year's rigorous imprisonment for offence under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of PFA Act read with Rule 50 of PFA Rules within a period of two months from today.
